lines.raw: Insurance in one sentence.

lines.raw: Many people put a little money into a shared pot every month.
lines.say: Many people put a little money into a shared pot every month.

lines.raw: When one of them gets sick, the pot pays most of the bill.
lines.say: When one of them gets sick, the pot pays most of the bill.

lines.raw: Nobody knows who will get sick, so everyone is protected.
lines.say: Nobody knows who will get sick, so everyone is protected.

lines.raw: That shared pot is **insurance**.
lines.say: That shared pot is insurance.

scenes.section: The money you pay to stay covered

lines.raw: Premium.
lines.say: Premium.

lines.raw: The regular fee you pay to **keep insurance active**, usually every month.
lines.say: The regular fee you pay to keep insurance active, usually every month.

lines.raw: You pay it whether you visit a doctor or not.
lines.say: You pay it whether you visit a doctor or not.

lines.raw: In the US, an employer often pays a large part of the premium and the worker pays the rest from their salary.
lines.say: In the U S, an employer often pays a large part of the premium and the worker pays the rest from their salary.

lines.raw: Policy.
lines.say: Policy.

lines.raw: The **contract** between the insurer and the person or company buying insurance.
lines.say: The contract between the insurer and the person or company buying insurance.

lines.raw: It lists what is covered, what is not, and the rules.
lines.say: It lists what is covered, what is not, and the rules.

lines.raw: Plan (health plan).
lines.say: Plan (health plan).

lines.raw: A specific **package of coverage** an insurer sells, with its own costs and rules.
lines.say: A specific package of coverage an insurer sells, with its own costs and rules.

lines.raw: One insurer may sell dozens of plans.
lines.say: One insurer may sell dozens of plans.

lines.raw: Emily's plan has the code `TXPPO1000`.
lines.say: Emily's plan has the code T X P P O 1 0 0 0.

lines.raw: Benefits.
lines.say: Benefits.

lines.raw: The **services the plan pays for**: doctor visits, hospital stays, medicines, lab tests and so on.
lines.say: The services the plan pays for: doctor visits, hospital stays, medicines, lab tests and so on.

lines.raw: "Is physiotherapy a covered benefit?" means "will the plan pay for it?"
lines.say: "Is physiotherapy a covered benefit?" means "will the plan pay for it?"

lines.raw: In Nepal: Ram and Sita pay to stay covered.

lines.raw: With private insurance:
lines.say: With private insurance:

lines.raw: Ram's startup buys a **group health policy** from an insurance company and pays a yearly **premium** for all its staff.
lines.say: Ram's startup buys a group health policy from an insurance company and pays a yearly premium for all its staff.

lines.raw: The **policy document** lists what is covered (for example hospital admission) and what is excluded (for example cosmetic treatment).
lines.say: The policy document lists what is covered (for example hospital admission) and what is excluded (for example cosmetic treatment).

lines.raw: If the premium is not paid and the policy is not renewed, Ram has no cover.
lines.say: If the premium is not paid and the policy is not renewed, Ram has no cover.

lines.raw: With the Social Security Fund:
lines.say: With the Social Security Fund:

lines.raw: Every month, part of Sita's salary, plus a contribution from her employer, goes to the **Social Security Fund (SSF)**.
lines.say: Every month, part of Sita's salary, plus a contribution from her employer, goes to the Social Security Fund (S S F).

lines.raw: That monthly contribution plays the same role as a **premium**: it keeps her covered.
lines.say: That monthly contribution plays the same role as a premium: it keeps her covered.

lines.raw: The SSF **guidelines** play the role of the **policy**: they say which services are covered and how much SSF pays.
lines.say: The S S F guidelines play the role of the policy: they say which services are covered and how much S S F pays.

lines.raw: Subscriber.
lines.say: Subscriber.

lines.raw: The person who **holds the coverage**, usually the employee.
lines.say: The person who holds the coverage, usually the employee.

lines.raw: Here, **Emily**.
lines.say: Here, Emily.

lines.raw: Also called the policyholder or primary insured.
lines.say: Also called the policyholder or primary insured.

lines.raw: Dependent.
lines.say: Dependent.

lines.raw: A family member covered **because of** the subscriber, usually a spouse or child.
lines.say: A family member covered because of the subscriber, usually a spouse or child.

lines.raw: Here, Emily's husband **Daniel** and daughter **Lily**.
lines.say: Here, Emily's husband Daniel and daughter Lily.

lines.raw: Member.
lines.say: Member.

lines.raw: **Anyone** covered by the plan: the subscriber **and** every dependent.
lines.say: Anyone covered by the plan: the subscriber and every dependent.

scenes.section: The two sides of every bill

lines.raw: Provider.
lines.say: Provider.

lines.raw: Anyone who **gives care**: a doctor, nurse, clinic, hospital, lab or pharmacy.
lines.say: Anyone who gives care: a doctor, nurse, clinic, hospital, lab or pharmacy.

lines.raw: Payer.
lines.say: Payer.

lines.raw: The organization that **pays for the care**: an insurance company, an employer's plan, or a government program like Medicare.
lines.say: The organization that pays for the care: an insurance company, an employer's plan, or a government program like Medicare.

lines.raw: Also called the **plan**, **carrier** or **insurer**.
lines.say: Also called the plan, carrier or insurer.

lines.raw: Insurer / carrier.
lines.say: Insurer or carrier.

lines.raw: A company in the business of insurance, such as a large US health insurer.
lines.say: A company in the business of insurance, such as a large U S health insurer.

lines.raw: "Carrier" is the same idea: it "carries" the risk.
lines.say: "Carrier" is the same idea: it "carries" the risk.

lines.raw: Self-funded (self-insured) plan.
lines.say: Self-funded (self-insured) plan.

lines.raw: A large employer pays claims **from its own money** and hires an insurer only to run the plan.
lines.say: A large employer pays claims from its own money and hires an insurer only to run the plan.

lines.raw: Emily's plan is the other kind, **fully insured**: the insurer takes the risk in return for the premium.
lines.say: Emily's plan is the other kind, fully insured: the insurer takes the risk in return for the premium.

lines.raw: Key takeaways.
lines.say: Key takeaways.

lines.raw: **Premium** = the regular fee to stay covered.
lines.say: Premium = the regular fee to stay covered.

lines.raw: It is never on a claim.
lines.say: It is never on a claim.

lines.raw: **Policy** = the contract; **plan** = the package of coverage; **benefits** = the services the plan pays for.
lines.say: Policy = the contract; plan = the package of coverage; benefits = the services the plan pays for.

lines.raw: **Subscriber** holds the coverage; **dependents** are covered through them; **members** = everyone covered.
lines.say: Subscriber holds the coverage; dependents are covered through them; members = everyone covered.

lines.raw: **Provider** gives care; **payer** pays for it.
